title: Spring-timing climate forecasts lost their gain when issued before the events, river-flow forecasts kept 74% at six months, and a lead-specific gate chose correctly in 36 of 40 tests
abstract: Question: do climate-response relations that kept forecast skill with observed weather still help when the forecast must be issued before the response, using only weather complete at the issue date, and can a training-only false-signal rate show the usable lead? Approach: we rebuilt ten campaign families (14,313 series; training to 2004, test 2005-2024) and reproduced their published results exactly at lead 0. In a timestamped plan, before any later result, we froze a lead-constrained refit (windows must end by the issue month, 0-6 months before the reference month-end), a climatology-fill alternative, the trend-preserving gate (FSR_T <= 0.32) recomputed at each lead, and seven hypotheses. Results: at lead 0, 79-96% of timing events had already occurred at issue. At lead 2, the first lead with at least 98.8% of events after issue, the climate gain over a 5-year trailing mean vanished for German spring phases (0.34 to -0.08) and cherry flowering (0.49 to -0.06) and fell for ice dates (0.45 to 0.07). Annual river flow kept 74% of its gain at 6 months. The lead-specific gate chose the better forecast in 12 of 16 units of signal families and 36 of 40 units overall, and beat the response-class rule (+0.042, 95% interval 0.036 to 0.048) and a gate that ignores lead (+0.010, 0.004 to 0.015). It did not locate the usable lead exactly (2 of 4 families). Refitting beat climatology fill (+0.086) except for rivers. Limitations: observed weather only, no seasonal forecasts, zero release lag, four signal families, lead-0 results known before the test.
